correctness.rationale: Every independent set is enumerated and checked against an independent row-transfer polynomial. A unit face-poset matching has its full directed Hasse graph exhaustively topologically sorted for n=1..6. Signed recursive gradient-path reductions construct integral Morse chain matrices; exact unimodular unit-pivot reductions finish with zero remainder and reveal all invariant factors (all 1). Morse boundary-square identities, independent raw mod-two boundary ranks at n<=5, and Euler characteristics also agree. n=3 has both H0=Z and H1=Z^2; the threshold refers specifically to at least two strictly positive dimensions. The theorem is finite and says only integral homology.

The 2007 matching-tree method is a technique, not the result for these graphs. The published four-cube independence complex is a different graph (Cartesian hypercube vs king Chebyshev grid), and the P6 categorical-product matching complex uses a different graph product and the matching rather than independence functor. The new threshold in multiple strictly positive homological degrees follows from the independently computed complete cases n<=5, not from a title mismatch.

originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected direct strong-product source, Carnero Bravo (2025), Section 5, Corollary 27 and Theorem 29, limits its family theorems to path-factor width at most four; no exact integral homology vector for the first square widths five and six appears there. Bousquet-Mélou–Linusson–Nevo (2007) study nearest-neighbor grid graphs, not king graphs with diagonal attacks. Searches by graph aliases, parameters, integer ranks, and coverage of stronger statements found no covering result; unindexed equivalent work remains a risk, so the PASS is a provisional scientific comparison, not a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: Potential unindexed or unpublished homology tables for the king graphs.
A future derivation from a stronger theorem not located in the inspected literature may cover the finite values.
Scientific assessment is not independent audit; proof checking is finite and exact for n<=6 only.

value.rationale: The widths five and six are precisely the first two square king boards beyond the directly relevant published strong-product treatment through width four, making a natural finite frontier rather than an arbitrary parameter choice. n=5 is the first square king board with nonzero reduced homology in multiple positive degrees, while n=6 has five consecutive nonvanishing degrees; full integral (torsion-sensitive) groups and their absence of torsion distinguish the result from placement-count enumerations and supply concrete benchmarks for the stronger graph-product topology problem.
